import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set a professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# using Stress Level to color and size the points. This helps to identify how stress influences
# sleep duration and quality combinations.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    size='Stress Level', # Map Stress Level to point size for additional emphasis
    sizes=(50, 400), # Define the range of sizes for the points, from smallest to largest
    palette='crest', # A sequential color palette, darker colors for higher stress levels
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency for overlapping points
    edgecolor='w', # Add a white edge to points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5 # Line width of the edge
)

# Add informative title and axis labels
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, and Stress Level', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Customize tick labels for better readability
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Position the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='Stress Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, frameon=True)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust plot layout to make space for the legend and prevent it from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.9, 1]) # rect=[left, bottom, right, top] in normalized figure coordinates

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
